provenance: PR #60 R1, second half. `near` returns from `_resolve_in` at the same point `index` does — before uniqueness and before the ambiguity bookkeeping — so a case-twin planted INSIDE the anchor's own row steals a proximity query from the element the plan meant. `case-twins.html` puts `SAVE FOR LATER` in Widget A's paragraph and `Save for later` further down; on `fbe304b` proximity picked the twin because the folded tier had gathered it as a candidate. Exact-first means the twin is not a candidate at all while an exact-case match exists, so proximity chooses among the elements the plan actually named.

Base `6b016b5` answers `The real save link`. As a case: `answer 'Twin inside Widget A' != expected 'The real save link'`. At the resolver: `['twin']` on fbe304b, `['real']` on base and after the fix.
triage.note: The document-order layout is load-bearing exactly as `forum-thread.html`'s is: moving the twin out of Widget A's paragraph disarms this case silently, because then the real link is nearest either way.
